# B2B

`sales.model.b2b` · model · parent `—`

> Selling to an organisation. Multiple people must agree, the buyer is not the user, and a formal process usually exists. The canonical capability set is closest to this motion, so this branch mostly emphasises rather than adds.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| buyer | an organisation, represented by a committee |
| typical_cycle_days | 60 |
| typical_acv | mid five to low six figures |
| committee_size | 3-7 seats |
| decision_style | consensus or committee vote, with an economic approver |
| primary_channels | `email`, `phone`, `linkedin`, `in_person` |


## Emphasises

- `sales.qualification.buying_committee_analysis`
- `sales.qualification.stakeholder_mapping`
- `sales.qualification.decision_maker_identification`
- `sales.closing.procurement`
- `sales.closing.legal_review`


## Extends `sales.obj.core.decision_maker`

Requires `approval_limit`, `authority_level`


> Approval limit is not optional in a B2B motion — a deal sized above an unverified limit is the most common cause of a slipped quarter.


## Extends `sales.obj.core.buying_committee`

Requires `size`, `roles_covered`


> Committee shape is the primary forecast input here.
